clue.text: Maybe fancies them to get married?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the word fancies could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a couple who fancy each other will wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals rearranging FANCIES; the definition reads the result as the people engaged to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged people are those promised to wed one another.

clue.text: Quarrel about radioactivity risk

explanation.surface: An argument over the dangers of nuclear radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out is to argue; radioactive dust settling after a nuclear blast is a hazard.

clue.text: Brief spoken interruption, coming from unusual angle?

explanation.surface: Someone butts in briefly from an odd direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the chance to speak at all is managing a short interjection; literally a word arriving sideways.

clue.text: Class given two notes-this shows their pitch

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
E and F are notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A music class learns two notes and the sign for their pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol at the start of a stave fixes the pitch of the notes written on it.

clue.text: Minced meat from America garnished with herb

indicators.note: garnished with means the America letters are surrounded by the herb, as a dish is dressed

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: An American dish of ground meat dressed with herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garnished with' reads like a cooking instruction but tells us the herb wraps around America.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is ground meat in a skin casing.

clue.text: From business, a lot of unselfish advice

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: a lot of the word, not all, so its tail end is dropped

explanation.surface: A firm offers some fairly generous guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' means most but not all of 'unselfish': its last four letters are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is formal guidance or recommendation given to someone.

clue.text: Man daily seen with another man

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day
Les is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is seen every day with another man.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' in Britain is a cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, borne by several kings.

clue.text: Our duty is to hold tongue

indicators.note: the words contain the answer inside them, as if holding it

explanation.surface: Duty demands we keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A language of Pakistan and India; tongue means language.

clue.text: Definitely not fast

parts.note: describes progress that is unhurried yet sure to arrive

explanation.surface: Someone insists a thing is in no way quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes gradual but steady progress towards a goal.

clue.text: Instrument ten played in alcove

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the instrument

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: played suggests the word ten is rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten musicians perform in a recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' signals the anagram of 'ten'; 'in' sets those letters inside the instrument, not in the alcove of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-moon recess or window in a wall or vault.

clue.text: Coolly appraised, on various levels?

explanation.surface: Someone is sized up disdainfully at different heights.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone from head to foot is a scornful appraisal; the phrase also playfully means having glanced at higher and lower floors.

clue.text: Chances of a contest

parts.note: the likelihood of each side winning a race or match, as quoted by bookmakers

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up who will win a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers' prices express the probability of each outcome in a sporting event.

clue.text: Set of data for board

explanation.surface: Information arranged neatly for a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Data laid out in rows and columns, and also a flat piece of furniture such as a dining surface (board as in bed and board).

clue.text: Large number meet black disgrace

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a lot is a large quantity

explanation.surface: Many people encounter shameful dishonour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on one's reputation is a mark of shame.

clue.text: Trophy I'd give blind boy

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone would award a trophy to a sightless lad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is depicted as a blindfolded boy with a bow.

clue.text: Hear singing group is in several papers

indicators.note: hear tells us the singing group word is said, not written

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: A choir appears in several newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A quire is twenty-four or twenty-five sheets of writing stock.

clue.text: Hair cut on top — not back, certainly

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word not in the opposite direction

parts.note: sure, as in 'sure, I'll come', means certainly

explanation.surface: A barber assures a client their crown has not been trimmed behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'not back' look like a remark about the haircut; 'back' actually reverses 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's shaven crown is a haircut of the top of the head.

clue.text: Trip and fall after a second

indicators.note: after places the word for fall behind the letter for a second

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a second of time
to tumble is to fall

explanation.surface: Someone trips and falls a moment later.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to lose one's footing, to blunder while walking.

clue.text: Doctor rejected a German painkiller

indicators.note: rejected suggests sent back, so the doctor word is read backwards

parts.note: DOC is a familiar word for a doctor
eine is German for 'a' (feminine)

explanation.surface: A German's doctor refused to prescribe analgesics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses the doctor word; 'a German' needs the German word for 'a', not an abbreviation for German.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate drug used to relieve pain and coughing.

clue.text: America and Russia's indisposition to fight?

definitions.text: America and Russia's indisposition to fight?

parts.words: America and Russia's indisposition to fight?
parts.note: an ailment such as a chill, plus a battle, describes the long superpower stand-off

explanation.surface: The two superpowers seem reluctant to go to battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The post-1945 rivalry between the USA and USSR stopped short of open combat.

clue.text: Perpetual ambition to get smaller

parts.note: an end is an aim or ambition
less means smaller

explanation.surface: An eternal wish to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: Never-stopping is the sense of something without limit.

clue.text: Sort of tortoise-like car?

parts.note: a tortoise has a rigid shell above it, so a car with a rigid roof is like it

explanation.surface: A motorist describes a slow vehicle as tortoise-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a fixed rigid roof, unlike a convertible.

clue.text: Hard to support greedy person with skill as artist

indicators.note: in a down answer, the letter below holds up the rest, so it supports them

parts.note: a hog is a greedy person
art is skill
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It is hard to back a greedy, skilful artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to support' puts H under HOG and ART.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and engraver.

clue.text: Urged publishers to take editor

parts.note: the press means publishers of newspapers

explanation.surface: Newspapers persuaded to take on an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushed someone to act, insisted.

clue.text: In general, potassium is the making of vegetable

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: Potassium is said, broadly, to make a vegetable what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'broadly' but gives the general LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An allium with long white stems, related to the onion, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Saw period beyond Christian era

indicators.note: beyond puts the period word after the era letters

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, labels years of the Christian era
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A historian dates something to after the birth of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb.

clue.text: Fool expected to receive small coin

indicators.note: to receive means the expected word takes the coin inside it

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at six
P stands for a penny, a small British coin

explanation.surface: A fool anticipates getting a little money.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or trick someone is to make a fool of them.

clue.text: Famous actor, a good man to lead a run

indicators.note: to lead puts the saint ahead of the other letters

parts.note: ST is a saint, a good man
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor heads a theatrical run.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading celebrity performer.

clue.text: Be on fire, reading Scots poet endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: Someone recites Robert Burns with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze is to be alight.

clue.text: Be somewhat suited to be dominant partner?

explanation.surface: Someone half-dressed in a suit is the boss at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing half a suit means donning its legs; the idiom means holding authority in a marriage.

clue.text: Puts holiday choices in different order

definitions.text: Puts holiday choices in different order

parts.words: Puts holiday choices in different order
parts.note: the word read with a hyphen means arranges again; as one word it means places to go on holiday

explanation.surface: A traveller rearranges a list of possible vacations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting again is rearranging, and seaside or ski towns are holiday destinations.

clue.text: Noble child looked sweet

parts.note: Hon, the Honourable, is a courtesy title of a nobleman's child
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's offspring gazed fondly.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are sugary and flattering are described as like bee nectar.
